cards.speaker: bram
cards.text: We hold three moorings below the Reach that the charter men have chained off for 'their timber'. There is no timber. We ask the gate whether a chain is a wall.

left.label: Cut the chain
left.outcome: "Then the gate is a gate today."

right.label: The Company's chain stays
right.outcome: "We remember chains. We have a long list."

cards.speaker: wren
cards.text: The town says a Hullfolk boy stole a ham from the Company store. He did. He's nine. The store's man wants him in the Book. The old man wants him fed. I want him to run faster.

left.label: The ham is paid for; no Book
left.outcome: You pay for a ham. The boy learns nothing and eats well.

right.label: In the Book, as anyone
right.outcome: The boy is in the Book. The Reach is very quiet about it.

cards.speaker: petronel
cards.text: The old woman on the gunwale sings a verse as your boat passes. A river, a hill, a door that closed. She stops when she sees you listening, and smiles, and does not start again.

left.label: Ask her to go on
left.outcome: "Another day. The river has more verses than I have breath."

right.label: Nod and move on
right.outcome: She sings again when your back is turned.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A Hullfolk boat is fishing the chamber itself, nets down, while the gate is closed for the night. The fish, they say, gather at the paddles. The Book says the chamber is not a fishery.

left.label: Nets up by first bell
left.outcome: They are. The fish are shared. Some come to your door.

right.label: Nets up now
right.outcome: They haul in, slowly, watching you.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The Reach is buying ale from a Sorrel barge instead of me. I don't blame them; I'd rather they bought mine. The moot wants the Sorrel barge told to move. It's moored on Company water.

left.label: Move the barge
left.outcome: Ilse sells more ale. The Reach drinks less of it.

right.label: Anyone may moor
right.outcome: "Anyone. Right. Remember that when it's the Company's barge."

cards.speaker: bram
cards.text: A charter man has been at the Reach with a measuring chain. He measured our boats. Nobody measures a boat that is going to stay. We ask what the gate knows.

left.label: Tell him about the Clearance review
left.outcome: "So. We have been here before. We hold."

right.label: The gate knows nothing
right.outcome: "The gate knows. The gate is choosing."

cards.speaker: wren
cards.text: The old man wants you at the Reach for the remembering. Names of the dead read out over the water, all night, no fire. He's never asked a Keeper. I told him you'd say no. Prove me wrong or don't.

left.label: Go
left.outcome: Forty names. Then a river's name. Nobody explains it.

right.label: Not this year
right.outcome: "Told him." She does not sound pleased to be right.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: Two Hullfolk boats have lashed together across the pound to settle a marriage dispute the old way: by argument, at volume, until dawn. Nothing can pass them. Nothing is trying to, yet.

left.label: Let them argue
left.outcome: By dawn they are married again and the pound is clear.

right.label: Separate them
right.outcome: Dace separates them. Both sides are furious with him instead.

cards.speaker: petronel
cards.text: The little fiddle has one string and I have one song. The charter men say the Reach is too loud at night. The Reach says the charter men are too quiet in the day. Which does the gate hear?

left.label: Play on
left.outcome: The town complains, then hums it.

right.label: Quiet after the last bell
right.outcome: She plays until the last bell exactly, and one note after.

cards.speaker: bram
cards.text: The town says a Hullfolk hand took a windlass from your lock house. We say the town's hands took it and blamed the water. We do not ask you to believe us. We ask you not to believe them first.

left.label: Search the Reach
left.outcome: No windlass. Forty silent people watching you look.

right.label: Search the lock house first
right.outcome: The windlass is behind the paddle gear. Dace goes red.

cards.speaker: wren
cards.text: One of ours is sick and Stroud won't come to the Reach without a Company chit. She's not being cruel. The Company made the rule. You could write the chit.

left.label: Write it
left.outcome: Stroud goes. She comes back angry at the rule, not at you.

right.label: Bring the sick one to the town
right.outcome: They carry her up. She lives. The Reach remembers the carrying.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A Hullfolk boat asks to tie up overnight in the chamber itself, out of the wind. It has a new baby aboard. It is against every rule in the Book and it would cost nothing.

left.label: In the chamber, till dawn
left.outcome: The gate is closed all night for one small boat.

right.label: The lee of the Company house
right.outcome: Out of the wind, within the rules. They take it.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: Bram Holloway's asked to speak at the moot. About moorings. The moot's never had a Hullfolk speak and half of it doesn't want to start. The other half wants to hear him refuse to say 'please'.

left.label: Let him speak
left.outcome: He speaks for ten minutes and does not say please. It goes better than anyone feared.

right.label: The moot is the town's
right.outcome: "It is. That's what I said. Didn't like saying it."

cards.speaker: bram
cards.text: The pound is low. When it is low the Reach touches bottom and we lie on our sides like the dead. We ask the gate for one less boat a day until the rain.

left.label: One less boat a day
left.outcome: The Reach floats. Pell counts the missing boat.

right.label: The boats come first
right.outcome: "They always have. We remember when they did not exist."

cards.speaker: wren
cards.text: Fine. The reed cargo. Sometimes it's not cheese. You knew that. What I'm asking is whether you want to know what it is, because once you know, you have to do something.

left.label: Tell me
left.outcome: "Rifles. Sorrel. Not many. Enough." She watches your face.

right.label: Don't tell me
right.outcome: "Smart. Sad, but smart."

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A Hullfolk elder has died at the Reach. They will take him down the west flight to a valley they do not name, and they ask for a Company boat to carry the body, since theirs are too small.

left.label: Lend the Company boat
left.outcome: The Company boat goes west with a Hullfolk crew and does not come back for a week.

right.label: Company boats are for Company work
right.outcome: They lash two boats and go. It takes them three days longer.

cards.speaker: petronel
cards.text: You have kind eyes for a charter man. Wren says you are not a charter man. I say everyone at the gate is one until they are not. Have a fish.

left.label: Have the fish
left.outcome: It is very good. She watches you eat it, satisfied.

right.label: Ask about the river in the song
right.outcome: "Which river?" There is only one, and she knows you know it.

cards.speaker: bram
cards.text: A charter man's dog drowned at the Reach. He says our children pushed it. Our children say it jumped for a fish. It was a good dog. We have laid it out. We ask nothing. He asks a great deal.

left.label: It jumped for a fish
left.outcome: The charter man is furious with you instead. It was, in fact, a fish.

right.label: The Reach pays for the dog
right.outcome: They pay in fish, as always. He does not want fish.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: Hullfolk children at the school door. Cole's building, Company lease, town's teacher. Nobody's said no yet because nobody's been asked. The teacher's asking you, since you're everyone's excuse.

left.label: Let them in
left.outcome: Six more in the schoolroom. Three town families take their children out. Then two put them back.

right.label: The school is the town's
right.outcome: "It's Cole's, actually. But yes."

cards.speaker: wren
cards.text: Bram won't ask, so I will. The Reach needs new mooring posts before winter. Tamm has timber. The Company has a rule about who Tamm can sell to. You have a pen.

left.label: Sign for the timber
left.outcome: Posts by winter. Vosk sees the chit and says nothing, which is louder than usual.

right.label: The rule is the rule
right.outcome: "The old man said you'd say that. I bet him you wouldn't. I owe him a fish."
